tagline: Down the creeks to the Snake, then into the gorge.
intro: West of Cambridge, Idaho 71 leaves the farmland and runs down Pine Creek and Brownlee Creek through remote, thinly settled country to the Snake River at Brownlee Dam. The route goes on to Oxbow, and from the Oxbow Bridge near Copperfield, Oregon, Hells Canyon Road follows the Idaho side of the river north.

This is the east side of Hells Canyon, North America's deepest river gorge, nearly 8,000 feet at its deepest. Pictographs and petroglyphs on its walls record the Nez Perce and the other peoples drawn here by its mild winters.

moments.title: Brownlee Dam
moments.text: The first of the three dams Idaho Power built in the canyon holds the Snake back in a reservoir 58 miles long, and Idaho 71 runs right past it.

moments.title: Hells Canyon Dam
moments.text: The road ends at the last of the three dams, and just below it, by the Hells Canyon Creek visitor center, the Snake begins its wild and scenic run.
